newsitem.title: USA: US June existing home sales dip seen as temporary.
newsitem.headline: US June existing home sales dip seen as temporary.

text.p: A decline in U.S. June existing home sales largely was expected by experts, but some expect lower interest rates to bolster sales down the road.

Existing home sales declined 2.6 percent to an annualized rate of 4.14 million. Economists surveyed by Reuters expected existing home sales to decline to 4.19 million from a revised 4.25 million units in May.
"Even though it did decline this month, we think underlying strength is good given high consumer confidence and declining mortgage rates," said Sung Won Sohn, chief economist at Norwest Corp.
A decline in the inventories of homes, though, offered some cheer to the housing industry.
According to the report, the months of supply declined to six months in June from May's 6.8 months.

The inventory levels were somewhat favorable, said Anothony Chan, chief economist at Banc One Investment Advisers of Columbus, Ohio. Chan noted that any number below six months tended to be associated with heightened activity in the months ahead.
Chan said, "Moving forward, we may fall below six months." He said the seasonally adjusted annual rate could climb above a 4.20-million-unit level.

Demand in the housing market, said Sohn, was particularly strong in the low to moderately priced segment. "Low to moderately priced homes are selling like hotcakes," he said, adding that the inventory number reflects a shortage of low to moderately priced homes.

John Mcauley, eonomist at Wilkinson Boyd Capital Markets, agreed that lower rates were sure to provide support to housing, but cautioned that low rates would not be the sole reason for consumers to buy a home. "This does not mean that people will jump in," he said.
According to the June report, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp's average commitment rate for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages was 7.69 percent, down from 7.94 percent in May.

Chan also noted that the existing home sales data compiled by the National Association of Realtors were a lagging indicator because more than 60 percent of existing home sales are contract closings. The other 40 percent of the existing sales are contract signings, said the Banc One economist.
Contract closings register when a consumer closes on a home; so, Chan said, 60 percent of home sales represent activity that has occurred in the last 60 to 90 days.
Norwest's Sohn said his firm's mortgage operation had already seen a pick-up in mortgage applications. "This would indicate that homes sales in the future will remain farily strong," he said.
Mcauley, meanwhile, questioned just how much upside there was to the existing home sales mart.

"The housing sector is at a fairly mature stage. You are not getting a lot of people moving around as you do at an early stage," he said, noting that existing home sales likely will linger at around an annualized 4.0- million-unit level.
